previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute chest pain and shortness of breath found to be due to a large saddle pulmonary embolism with right heart strain. He had been off antiplatelet therapy in preparation for hernia surgery, which likely contributed to the clot formation. He was initially managed with heparin and then received tPA for clot dissolution, after which his symptoms resolved. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout. His anticoagulation was transitioned to Coumadin and Lovenox. A flare of chronic back pain was managed with pregabalin, OxyContin, and adjuvant therapies; MRI showed post-surgical changes without acute pathology. His diabetes, heart failure, and other comorbidities were monitored and managed. He was discharged home with services on anticoagulation for at least six months and follow-up plans for cardiology, primary care, and pain management.
